name: Moeller Attack — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Moeller Attack. Find the winning 2-move sequence from the critical Moeller positions.

drills.name: The e-file Pin & Overload
drills.description: White retreats the rook to e1 to double on the e-file, then centralises the queen on e2 to add decisive pressure on the pinned knight.
drills.briefExplanation: Re1 reloads the rook on the open e-file. When Black centralises the knight, Qe2 adds overwhelming pressure.
drills.explanation: After Re1, White doubles major pieces on the e-file. If Black plays Nf5, Qe2 piles on the pressure immediately. White now threatens Bf4, d6, and Rxe7 simultaneously — Black cannot meet all threats. The knight on g5 eyes f7 while the e-file battery targets the unprotected Ne7. White has a crushing initiative.

drills.name: The f7 Knight Sacrifice
drills.description: White sacrifices the knight on f7, ripping open the black king's defences and winning back material with the e-file rook.
drills.briefExplanation: Nxf7 tears apart Black's kingside. After Rxf7, White wins the knight on e7 with the rook.
drills.explanation: After Nxf7 Rxf7, White plays Rxe7! The rook crashes into e7, winning the knight outright. Black has no good reply — the queen on d8 is attacked, and after Qxe7 White continues with Qd3 and Bc4 pressure on f7. White recovers material with a continuing attack. The open e-file was the key — every Moeller position revolves around it.

drills.name: The d6 Breakthrough
drills.description: White advances the d-pawn to d6, cramping Black's position. After Black captures the pawn, White occupies the e-file with the rook.
drills.briefExplanation: d6 wedges deep into Black's position. After Nxd6, Re1 puts the rook on the open file attacking the exposed knight.
drills.explanation: After d6, Black is forced to capture with Nxd6 (allowing the knight to be targeted). Re1 seizes the e-file and eyes the exposed Nd6 immediately. White follows with Bf4 and Qd2, creating a powerful passed pawn and attacking the e7-knight simultaneously. The d6-pawn disrupts Black's queenside coordination and gives White a lasting initiative.

drills.name: The Bg5 Pin Exploitation
drills.description: White pins the bishop on f6 to the queen with Bg5, then captures to damage Black's pawn structure and target the kingside.
drills.briefExplanation: Bg5 pins the bishop on f6 to the queen. Even after h6, White takes anyway — the structural damage is worth it.
drills.explanation: Bg5 pins the Bf6 to the queen on d8. Even if Black tries h6 to drive the bishop away, Bxf6 is played regardless — the bishop pair is surrendered in exchange for wrecking Black's kingside pawn structure. White follows with Qh5 and Re1, targeting h7 and f7 for a decisive kingside attack. The advanced d5-pawn and active rook combine for overwhelming pressure.
